sourceReasoning: Each classic file script dispatches only through its own document.currentScript property; the per-element handler additionally requires the original worker, live owner and exact current script element. It cannot route an obsolete payload through a replacement global.

Cleanup removes that script handler and both load/error handlers before removal, cancels the sole continuation timer and removes the pending DOMContentLoaded callback. Captured old load/error closures independently reject the stale worker/element.

The embedded path invokes the same guarded accept function directly, retains inert payloads for retry, and schedules further chunks only while its worker remains current. HTTP boot/fetch and accepted-surface authority are unchanged.
Transport metadata/order/type checks remain, with an additional duplicate-per-script rejection. No size, atob, byte-order or asset-digest validation is weakened.
One script and one continuation timer are owned at a time; no new permanent callback registry or global no-op sink is introduced.
